checkout.label: Payments
checkout.name: Build a checkout
checkout.summary: Take USDC, a digital dollar, from anyone with a wallet. You can use the money in under a second, the fee is a fraction of a cent, and there are no chargebacks.
steps: Pay for something the way your customers will, before writing any code.
Edit the code behind the payment and take your first payment with it.
Ship the order only after your server has checked the payment on the network itself.
Switch to mainnet, decide who pays network fees, and handle the edge cases real customers hit.

after.title: Explore the payments guides
after.summary: Send payments, subscriptions, deferred execution, and more.

demo.title: Demo Sticker Shop
demo.success: Verified. The shop's server confirmed that 1 USDC for order-1001 reached the shop, so the order can ship.

steps.label: The customer pays 1 USDC
steps.description: The order asks for 1,000,000 base units (1 USDC) and carries a fresh reference. The customer's wallet approves one USDC transfer to the shop, and `payStore` returns the transaction's signature. The shop hasn't checked anything yet.

steps.label: The shop's server verifies the payment
steps.description: The checkout sends the signature to the shop's server. The server fetches that transaction from the network and checks that it succeeded, carries the order's reference, and moved exactly 1 USDC of the USDC mint into the shop's account. Only then is the order paid.

checks.title: What a wrong amount looks like

steps.label: Check the payment against a 2 USDC price
steps.description: The same 1 USDC payment, checked against an order that costs 2 USDC. `verifyPayment` refuses it, so the shop wouldn't ship.

paywall-api.label: Pay-per-call
paywall-api.name: Paywall an endpoint
paywall-api.summary: Price each request at a fraction of a cent. Clients, whether people's apps or AI agents, pay inline over HTTP, with no signup, API key or invoice.
steps: Watch the HTTP 402 flow happen: request, price, payment, data.
One middleware, a price, and your wallet address.
Install the middleware in your own app, pick a facilitator, and pay for your endpoint from a real client.
Mainnet, a facilitator you trust, and protection for unpaid routes.

after.title: More about pay-per-call
after.summary: Facilitators, pricing models, and agent payments.

demo.title: Paid forecast API · 0.001 USDC per request
demo.success: Paid 0.001 USDC and got the forecast. No signup, no API key.

steps.label: Call the API without paying
steps.description: The server answers *402 Payment Required* with the price (1000 base units, 0.001 USDC) and the address to pay.

steps.label: Pay and call again
steps.description: The client signs a 0.001 USDC payment and sends the same request again with it in the `X-PAYMENT` header. The server settles the payment onchain and answers with the forecast.

checks.title: Requests that don't get the forecast

steps.label: Send the same payment again
steps.description: The same `X-PAYMENT` header a second time gets 402: one payment buys one response.

steps.label: Call with a cap below the price
steps.description: A client that pays at most 500 base units (0.0005 USDC) sees the 0.001 USDC price and signs nothing.

issue-asset.label: Tokenized asset
issue-asset.name: Issue an asset
issue-asset.summary: Create a token for a fund share, a security, or a real-world asset, with metadata, an approval list and a pause switch that the network enforces on every transfer.
steps: Approve an investor, send LSF to them and to an unapproved account, and watch the network enforce the rule.
Create a Token-2022 mint with metadata, a pause switch, and default-frozen accounts.
Create the same asset from your terminal, then approve a holder so they can receive it.
Protect the authority keys, connect your KYC process, and decide who can pause.

after.summary: Token extensions, compliance controls, and delivery vs payment.

demo.title: Lisbon Solar Fund (LSF) · restricted asset
demo.success: The approved investor received 100 LSF, and the network blocked the 1 LSF transfer to the unapproved account. The issuer then paused and resumed the asset, and moved 50 LSF out of the approved investor's account.

steps.label: Approve two investors
steps.description: Every new LSF token account opens frozen. The issuer opens and approves (thaws) two investor accounts: the first now holds 1000 LSF, the second 0 LSF.

steps.label: Send to an approved and an unapproved account
steps.description: The holder (the first investor) sends 100 LSF to the approved investor, and it confirms. Sending 1 LSF to an account nobody approved, still frozen, fails onchain with `Custom: 17` (*Account is frozen*), and with preflight it is rejected before it lands.

steps.label: Pause, resume, and claw back
steps.description: The issuer pauses the asset, which blocks every transfer (`Custom: 67`), and resumes it. As permanent delegate it then moves 50 LSF out of the approved investor's account without their signature.
